text:
Maria (People Ops): heads-up: multiple hiring managers noticed final candidate scores look lower than expected after yesterday's rubric push. anyone on recruiting seeing a spike in low aggregate scores?
Sam (Recruiting Ops): seeing it. Quick glance shows many scorecards are missing the new "impact" dimension; total_score is computed from 4 dims but UI shows 5, so averages are inconsistent. :frowning:
Ivy (Hiring Manager): we had a 4.2 -> 3.1 drop on a candidate who seemed fine during interviews. This is blocking offers tonight.
Lee (Recruiter): Same here. I noticed the score variance after the new rubric (v2.1) shipped. Some interviewers got v2.0 and some v2.1 templates.
Ben (Data Eng): likely a versioning race. Our score aggregation job expects schema with fields [skill, culture, role, impact, logistics] when rubric_version = "v2.1". If template saved without "impact" the aggregator treats it as zero.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): can we quickly detect which interviews used which template? I can pull by interview ids but need a script.
Ben (Data Eng): I can query interview_scorecards table: SELECT interview_id, rubric_version, json_keys(payload) FROM interview_scorecards WHERE created_at >= '2026-03-24'; that'll show mismatched keys.
qa-bot: alert.score-variance  recent_window=1h affected_interviews=27
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Ok rolled up: 27 interviews used v2.0 payloads; aggregator ran for them with v2.1 rules. That's why totals dropped.
Ivy (Hiring Manager): urgent: can we recalc totals for those 27 using the v2.0 rules? We need to restore the scores for offer approvals.
Ben (Data Eng): yes. I'll run a recalculation job that respects rubric_version per row. Pseudo: for each scorecard, if rubric_version='v2.0' use weights_v2_0 else weights_v2_1. Backfill will update candidate_totals. I'll run in read-only first and show diffs.
Lee (Recruiter): please prioritize the 6 interviews for today (ids: I-3120, I-3133, I-3155, I-3160, I-3181, I-3190). Those are blocking offers.
Ben (Data Eng): noted. I'll run targeted recalcs for those 6 now, then full backfill for 27.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): also we should stop the nightly aggregator until we confirm it's version-aware. I can flip a feature flag to pause aggregator job.
Maria (People Ops): do it. Pause the job and coordinate the fast-path backfill.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): paused aggregator (flag=score_aggregator_running=false) for all orgs.
Ben (Data Eng): recalculated the 6 urgent interviews. Diffs: 4 candidates increased by 0.8-1.1 points restoring them above offer threshold. Applying updates now for those.
Ivy (Hiring Manager): confirmed two offers can proceed. thank you.
Ben (Data Eng): full backfill for the other 21 queued; will run in 10m batches and post progress. Also pushing a code fix to aggregator to look at rubric_version per scorecard (making weight lookup explicit).
qa-bot: ci.pipeline  job=fix/aggregator-version-check status=running
Sam (Recruiting Ops): I'll add a checklist step to release notes: when changing rubric schema, deploy aggregator patch and run compatibility check before shipping.
Maria (People Ops): good. can we also surface rubric_version in the interviewer UI so interviewers know which template they're using? small UX change request.
Lee (Recruiter): helpful for training teams. also reaching out to interviewers who used v2.0 to ask for any free-text notes that might be missing.
Ben (Data Eng): backfill finished for the 27, no failures. Pushed aggregator fix to staging; QA running tests.
qa-bot: ci.pipeline  job=fix/aggregator-version-check status=passed
Sam (Recruiting Ops): plan: merge fix, deploy to prod behind flag, run compatibility check job, unpause aggregator. I'll schedule a 30m maintenance window.
Maria (People Ops): excellent. action items recap: Ben ran recalcs (done), Sam to deploy aggregator fix and update onboarding checklist, Lee to notify interviewers, Maria to update hiring leads. Moving to follow-up; will reopen if anything else pops up.
